description: The first saved-workflow compatibility attempt stopped after the original verifier passed its first parent: JavaScript deep comparison distinguished returned -0 from 0 in the retained JSON receipt. The harness now compares both in the receipt's JSON representation, where serialization canonicalizes -0 to 0. The failed result, log, earlier harness and preliminary locks are retained in the external evidence. A subsequent lock-only correction excludes the lock document from its own hash inventory. The first fresh application session passed all ten tasks. The initial historical audit was then stopped because Git mapped about 14.6 GB into its working set. Git object windows are now explicitly capped at 128 MiB, 16 MiB per window, with 32 MiB delta cache. The same full audit was restarted, archive tests repeated, and a second full app session run under a new lock. Both earlier fresh sessions passed. The first small clone built successfully, but an independent exact-source check found 311 originally tracked log files omitted by ordinary git add and current ignore rules. The export now force-adds only the explicit tracked inventory inside its new disposable directory. The first clone and refusal are retained; a new clone is built and every selected source blob compared. The final app session is repeated under the corrected tool lock; reported final comparison uses on-c. The final saved-workflow check passes all ten parents. No source, outcome or acceptance tolerance was relaxed.
